title: Latvia: crossing attempts from Belarus already above all of 2025
summary: Latvia's border guard says 12,857 people were stopped trying to cross from Belarus between 1 January and 10 November 2026, compared with 12,046 in all of 2025, 5,388 in 2024 and 13,863 in 2023. On 12 November the interior ministry proposed extending the enhanced border regime in Ludza, Krāslava, Augšdaugava and Daugavpils areas until 30 June 2027, citing continued pressure, tunnels and damage to border equipment.
corroboration: LETA figures via UA.NEWS and BNN; daily figures from LSM.
analysis: The year-to-date figure counts prevented attempts, not people, so the same person may be counted more than once. Even so, the trend is clear and matches the Commission's view that pressure has shifted from Poland to Latvia.

title: Latvian prosecutors: migrants forced to damage border equipment
summary: Latvian prosecutors say migrants waiting on the Belarusian side were told to damage Latvian border infrastructure or face violence if they could not pay about 5,000 dollars for a crossing, and that there are reasonable suspicions of involvement by Belarusian border officials. More than 60 cases of damage were recorded this year, against 23 last year. On 10 November border guards caught a Belarusian driver carrying seven people who had crossed illegally; Latvia has raised the maximum penalty for organising illegal migration to 12 years.
corroboration: LSM and LTV De facto, via UA.NEWS; LSM report of 11 November.
analysis: This is the clearest sign that pressure on Latvia is organised rather than spontaneous. Statements about Belarusian officials come from an ongoing investigation and have not been tested in court.

title: EU solidarity: the Baltic states are at risk, and no one can be forced to take people
summary: The Commission's annual report of 6 November lists Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Finland as at risk of migratory pressure, which gives them priority EU support, and allows Estonia and five other countries to ask for their 2027 contribution to be reduced. Greece, Cyprus, Italy and Spain are the countries under pressure that receive help. For 2026 the EU agreed 21,000 relocations or equivalent support and 420 million euros, and each country chooses how to contribute. The Council is now negotiating the 2027 pool.
corroboration: European Commission report; Council of the EU; Euronews; Bytes Europe.
analysis: The rules work against forced redistribution to the Baltic states. Euronews reports that fewer than 1,000 people will actually be relocated across the EU in 2026, with most countries paying instead.

title: Poland keeps checks on the Lithuanian border until March 2027
summary: On 1 October Poland extended its checks on the borders with Lithuania and Germany for six months, to 30 March 2027. It says nearly 1,300 people have been refused entry at the Lithuanian border since July 2025 and more than 130 detained for helping illegal crossings.
corroboration: Polish interior ministry; Anadolu-based report.
analysis: This is the main way neighbouring EU countries are pushing pressure back toward Lithuania. It is lawful under Schengen rules for a limited time, but it has now been renewed several times.

title: Estonia closes road crossings with Russia from 1 December
summary: Estonia will close the Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula road crossings after a sabotage attempt it attributes to Russia. Its prime minister says border guards are prepared for a possible attempt to push migrants across, as happened at Finland's border in 2023.
corroboration: ERR, Al Jazeera and others.
analysis: The closure is a security response, but it raises the risk that Russia tries to send migrants toward the green border, as it did with Finland. No such movement has been reported yet.

title: Returns under EU rules are aimed at Italy and Greece, not the Baltics
summary: Germany says returns to Italy and Greece under the EU rules should resume for people who arrived after the Pact took effect on 12 June 2026. No reports were found of Germany or other western countries planning returns to the Baltic states. Within the region, Lithuania returns people who entered through Latvia under a three-country agreement.
corroboration: Il Sole 24 Ore; LRT.
analysis: People who first entered the EU through the Baltic states can lawfully be sent back there. This indicator will show if that starts to grow.

title: Lithuania moves to pay rather than take relocated migrants
summary: On 16 November Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas said a government commission had approved his proposal that Lithuania contribute to the EU solidarity pool by paying rather than accepting relocated migrants; the government still has to approve it, and the amount is not yet clear. In December 2025 Lithuania had planned to accept half of its share and pay for the rest, and in May 2026 it agreed to take 58 asylum seekers from Cyprus and pay 1.4 million euros, followed by a memorandum with Cyprus in June.
corroboration: LRT; the Cyprus agreement was reported by LRT and Cyprus Mail.
analysis: The change shows the scheme working as designed: each country chooses how to contribute. It is not clear whether any of the 58 people have already arrived or what happens to that pledge; this edition will track it.

title: Estonia debates checks on its Latvian border
summary: Estonian opposition parties Centre and EKRE want checks on the border with Latvia, citing saboteurs and illegal migrants who came through Latvia; Isamaa is conditionally open. The governing Reform and Eesti 200 parties and the Social Democrats oppose them. Interior Minister Igor Taro said the government is far from considering checks, which he estimated would cost about 300 million euros, and the president said she sees no reason for them.
corroboration: ERR; earlier police figures reported by Reform.news.
analysis: Estonian police detained 149 people for illegal migration in the first half of 2026, many believed to have come via Belarus and Latvia, so the concern is real, but checks inside the Baltics would mostly slow onward movement rather than stop pressure at the external border.

title: Belarus border: Lithuania's turn-backs already above 2025, Poland extends its buffer zone
summary: Lithuania's border guard service had turned back 1,896 people from Belarus by 7 November, more than the 1,652 in all of 2025 and the 1,002 in 2024, though far below Latvia's figures. Poland recorded 482 attempts at its Belarus border by 8 November, and its interior ministry published a draft on 14 November to extend the restricted zone along part of the border until 27 February 2027, citing balloons and drones from Belarus used for smuggling.
corroboration: Lithuanian figures via BNS and regional media; Polish figures via Defence24.
analysis: These are catch-up figures from early November, not new events. They show pressure spread across all three countries, with Latvia the main target and Poland now much quieter than in 2021–2024.

title: Five EU states plan a Rwanda return hub; Estonia backs it but stays out
summary: Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece announced on 16 November that they are working with Rwanda on a hub for people who have no right to stay in Europe and have exhausted appeals, with about 100 people to be sent at first from 2027 under the EU's new return rules. Estonia supports the initiative but will not join it. Rights groups and some MEPs criticise the plan and expect court challenges.
corroboration: ERR, the Dutch government and Euronews.
analysis: This concerns returns outside the EU, not moving people between EU states, so it does not shift migrants onto the Baltic states.

title: Lithuanian minister rejects xenophobia accusations over refusing relocations
summary: On 18 November Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas rejected accusations of xenophobia and racism after announcing that Lithuania will accept no migrants under the EU solidarity mechanism next year and pay into the bloc's fund instead. He said the decision is political and financial and that paying would be cheaper over an estimated five years; the amount has not been set. This year Lithuania agreed to take 58 people from Cyprus and pay €1.4 million.
corroboration: Reported by LRT; the government commission's approval was reported on 16 November.
analysis: The move is lawful under the Pact and is a national choice, not something imposed by Brussels. The cost argument cannot be checked yet, and the shift from a mixed approach this year to payment only next year is a political decision that rights groups are likely to contest.

title: Quiet days in Lithuania, dozens of attempts in Latvia
summary: Lithuania's border guard service recorded no attempts to cross from Belarus outside official points on 15–17 November, the third day in a row, after turning back seven people on 14 November; its total for 2026 is 1,962, above the 1,652 for all of 2025. Latvia's border guard reported 12 attempts on 14 November, 41 on 15 November, 29 on 16 November and 6 on 17 November.
corroboration: Figures from the two border guard services, reported by BNS and LSM and summarised by Bytes Europe.
analysis: Latvia remains the main pressure point. A few quiet days in Lithuania do not show a lasting change: the numbers swing with weather and with where organisers send groups, and they count attempts, not people.

title: Estonia: Latvian border checks would cost €65 million and are not needed now
summary: Estonia's Interior Ministry secretary general Tarmo Miilits said on 18 November that restoring checks on the Latvian border would cost about €65 million, that there is no security need for them today and that the police could restore them fairly quickly if needed. He argued the money would be better spent doubling patrols and strengthening counterintelligence, and said agencies are prepared for possible Russian retaliation through illegal migration once the eastern crossings close. The same day parliament backed the bill to close crossings with Russia in first reading, 37 to 2.
corroboration: Reported by ERR, LSM, APA and TASS.
analysis: The government position weakens the case made by opposition parties for checks inside Schengen, but the gap between this figure and the roughly €300 million cited earlier in the week shows the cost debate is not yet settled.

title: Estonian court case shows the onward route from Latvia
summary: ERR reported on 16 November that Harju County Court convicted a 24-year-old Egyptian man in August, under a plea bargain, for driving five migrants from Bangladesh and Algeria from Latvia into Estonia in an unregistered van with false plates. He admitted being paid, and was sentenced to one year in prison, expulsion and a six-year entry ban. Officials link such cases to the hybrid attack on the Belarus–Latvia border.
corroboration: Reported by ERR from court information.
analysis: A single, older case, but it illustrates the onward movement behind the Estonian debate on checks at the Latvian border. Such transport within Schengen is a criminal matter for police, separate from returns of migrants between EU states.

title: Latvia's prevented crossings pass 13,000 for the year
summary: Latvia's State Border Guard reported 29 prevented attempts on 16 November, bringing the 2026 total to about 13,012, more than the 12,046 for all of 2025 and close to the 2023 record of 13,863. Another 6 attempts followed on 17 November. Latvia has extended its reinforced border regime in five municipalities until the end of the year.
corroboration: Border guard figures carried by LETA, Diena and Reform.news; counted once.
analysis: The record is a measure of attempts, not people, and officials acknowledge repeat attempts; it shows sustained organised pressure on Latvia rather than a new surge.

title: Baltic states' status in the EU solidarity system: 'at risk', not exempt
summary: The Commission's 6 November assessment named Cyprus, Greece, Italy and Spain as under migratory pressure and eligible for the 2027 solidarity pool. It listed 15 states as at risk, including Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, giving them priority access to EU support, and six states, including Estonia and Poland, as facing a significant migratory situation, which lets them ask the Council to reduce their contributions. The Council is expected to set the pool's size and each state's share before the end of the year.
corroboration: Reported by Bernama and VisaVerge from the Commission's annual report.
analysis: Reports that Poland and Estonia are 'exempt' overstate the position: they may request deductions, which the Council must still decide. Nothing in the designations obliges any Baltic state to take relocated migrants.

title: Lithuania plans a fence on parts of the Kaliningrad border
summary: Lithuania's border guard service has drawn up a plan to reinforce the border with Kaliningrad, including a segmented barbed-wire fence on selected stretches. The interior minister said more money is needed and linked army help at the border to a possible Russian mobilisation after the Duma elections.
corroboration: Reported by LRT and European Pravda.
analysis: The plan is mainly about hybrid threats and possible draft evaders from Russia, not a current migration flow; officials say the threat level has not risen.

title: Estonia has returned over 400 people to Latvia this year
summary: ERR reported that more than 400 migrants caught in Estonia this year after travelling from Latvia were returned there, and that 11 people have been detained on suspicion of smuggling. A court sentenced a 24-year-old foreign man to a year in prison for driving five migrants from Latvia to Estonia.
corroboration: Police and prosecution figures reported by ERR.
analysis: These are lawful returns between neighbouring states for people who entered via Belarus, not western European states shifting migrants onto the Baltic states.

title: Estonia formally approves closing its road crossings with Russia
summary: Estonia's government approved closing the Narva-1, Narva-2, Koidula, Luhamaa and Saatse road checkpoints from 1 December, with a review after six months; rail traffic continues. The government cites the 14 November sabotage attempt it links to Russian military intelligence. Russia's foreign ministry called it a new Iron Curtain and promised political and diplomatic measures.
corroboration: Reported by Euronews and Reuters (via the Moscow Times).
analysis: The closure is a security measure, not a migration one, and no migrant movement has been reported on the Russian side. Estonia's contingency planning for a possible push of migrants afterwards is a precaution, not evidence of one.

title: How many people has Estonia returned to Latvia?
summary: ERR reported on 3 November that 388 irregular migrants had been found in Estonia this year, of whom 148 were handed back to Latvia under EU rules, and 15 people had been detained on suspicion of smuggling. The head of the northern border guard bureau said only 14 migrants were caught in the last week of October and expects numbers to rise next spring as the route has shifted north.
corroboration: Police figures reported by ERR; our 20 November edition gave 'over 400 returned', which appears to have conflated people caught with people returned.
analysis: These are lawful returns between neighbours of people who entered the EU via Belarus. They are a consequence of Belarus's route, not of western European states shifting migrants onto the Baltic states.

title: No new border figures since 17 November
summary: The latest published figures found are Latvia's 29 prevented attempts on 16 November and 6 on 17 November, bringing its year total to about 13,018, and Lithuania's three days without attempts on 15–17 November. Lithuania's year total, about 1,962, is already above the roughly 1,650 recorded in 2025.
corroboration: Border guard figures as carried by Reform.news and The New Backyard; counted once.
analysis: Gaps in publication are common and do not mean crossings stopped. Totals count attempts, and the same people often try repeatedly.

title: EU's 2027 solidarity pool still pending
summary: The Council has not yet adopted the 2027 solidarity pool. Last year the 2026 pool was politically approved on 8 December and then adopted by written procedure. Under the Commission's 6 November assessment the Baltic states are 'at risk', giving them priority access to EU support.
corroboration: Commission assessment as reported earlier this month; the 2025 timetable reported by Agence Europe.
analysis: If the Council follows last year's timetable, a decision is likely in December. Nothing in the rules obliges any Baltic state to accept relocated migrants; states can pay or give other support instead.

title: EU officials examine the 2027 solidarity pool
summary: The High-Level EU Solidarity Forum met in Brussels on 20 November. Its agenda covered the Commission's proposal for the 2027 solidarity pool and a draft decision letting member states facing a significant migratory situation reduce their contributions. Both documents are classified, and no outcome has been published.
corroboration: Council agenda document; no press reporting on the outcome found.
analysis: This is the step before the Council adopts the pool; last year that came on 8 December. Under the rules states may relocate people, pay or offer other support, so no Baltic state can be made to accept migrants. Whether Estonia or Poland get deductions is the open question.

title: Estonia's returns to Latvia: two ERR figures that do not match
summary: ERR reported on 3 November that 148 of 388 people found in Estonia this year had been handed back to Latvia. In a 16 November report on a smuggling conviction, ERR said over 400 migrants had been caught this year and are then returned to Latvia. In our 21 November edition we concluded that only about 150 had been returned; that was too firm.
corroboration: Both figures come from police data as reported by ERR; no official breakdown of returns found.
analysis: The difference may be timing or wording, so we now rate the 'over 400 returned' figure as contested rather than wrong. Either way these are lawful returns between neighbours of people who entered the EU via Belarus.

title: Latvia: 3 attempts on 18 November, about 13,021 this year
summary: Latvia's State Border Guard reported stopping 3 people trying to cross from Belarus on 18 November, bringing the year's total to about 13,021. No later daily figures were found. The guard has opened 138 criminal cases over people smuggling this year.
corroboration: Latvian border guard daily report; counted once.
analysis: Low daily numbers in November follow a much heavier summer. Totals count attempts, and the same people often try repeatedly, so the year total overstates the number of people.

title: Russia's northern borders: Estonia closes, Finland stays shut
summary: Estonia's five road crossings with Russia close on 1 December, a decision taken over sabotage concerns. Finland's land border with Russia has been closed since December 2023, and its government plans to extend until the end of 2028 the law that allows asylum applications at the border to be restricted in exceptional cases.
corroboration: Estonian decision reported earlier this week; Finnish plan reported by Hromadske in September.
analysis: Both are security measures. Rights groups have criticised Finland's law; no migrant movement toward either border has been reported.

title: Human rights court to rule tomorrow on pushbacks at the Belarus border
summary: The European Court of Human Rights says its Grand Chamber will deliver rulings on 24 November in three cases: A.R. and Others v. Poland (Afghan nationals stranded at the border in 2021), H.M.M. and Others v. Latvia (Iraqi Kurds allegedly pushed back from August 2021) and C.O.C.G. and Others v. Lithuania (four Cubans who crossed in 2022). Hearings were held in February 2025.
corroboration: Announced on the court's own website.
analysis: The rulings will shape how far Baltic and Polish border laws can go in a situation Belarus uses for pressure. Governments argue instrumentalisation justifies tougher rules; rights groups argue the right to seek asylum still applies. Both sides are likely to claim parts of the judgment; we will report what the court actually decides.

title: Finland extended its border law to 2028 (correction)
summary: Finland's parliament voted 170 to 19 on 18 November to extend until the end of 2028 the law that allows asylum applications at the Russian border to be refused in exceptional cases. Prime Minister Petteri Orpo called it essential; critics say it conflicts with the constitution and the ban on returning people to danger. Our earlier editions wrongly said the extension was still pending.
corroboration: Yle reporting carried by several outlets; the vote count comes from one syndicated report.
analysis: The law has not been used since the border closed in December 2023; its extension is preparation for a possible push from Russia rather than a response to current arrivals.

title: No new border figures since 18 November
summary: We found no new official daily figures from Latvia or Lithuania after 18 November. Latvia's latest totals put prevented attempts this year at about 13,000, with 29 on 16 November and 3 on 18 November; Lithuania reported none on 15–17 November and about 1,962 this year.
corroboration: Border guard figures as relayed by LSM, Reform.news and The New Backyard; slightly different year totals reflect different cut-off dates.
analysis: Gaps in publication are normal, especially at weekends; they are not evidence that crossings have stopped. Figures count attempts, not people.

title: 2027 solidarity pool: decision expected before year-end
summary: After the 20 November forum, the Council is expected to set the 2027 solidarity pool before the end of 2026. Four southern states are under migratory pressure; Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia are among 15 states 'at risk', giving them priority access to EU support, and Estonia is among six that may ask for reduced contributions. States can relocate people, pay €20,000 per person not relocated, or give other support.
corroboration: European Commission designations of 6 November, summarised by VisaVerge and Bernama.
analysis: Nothing in the process obliges a Baltic state to accept migrants; each chooses how to contribute. The open question is the size of each state's share, which the Council has not published.

title: Human rights court rules today on Belarus-border pushbacks
summary: The European Court of Human Rights' Grand Chamber delivers its rulings today in three cases on summary returns at the Belarus border in 2021–2022: A.R. and Others v. Poland, H.M.M. and Others v. Latvia and C.O.C.G. and Others v. Lithuania. The outcome was not public when this edition was written.
corroboration: Announced on the court's own website.
analysis: The judgments will test whether laws allowing people to be turned back at a border that Belarus uses for pressure are compatible with the European Convention on Human Rights. Governments and rights groups will each claim parts of the ruling; we will report what the court actually decides.

title: Russia protests Estonia's border closure
summary: Russia's foreign ministry summoned Estonia's chargé d'affaires on 23 November to protest the closure of Estonia's road crossings with Russia from 1 December for at least six months, and said Tallinn's actions were bringing the situation to the brink of open war. Estonia rejected the accusations.
corroboration: Reported by Reuters, AFP, The Moscow Times and Meduza from the same ministry statement.
analysis: The closure is a security response to sabotage, not a migration measure, but Estonia's interior ministry has warned Russia could push migrants toward its border. No such movement has been reported.

title: Latvia: 179 criminal proceedings over illegal movement of people this year
summary: Latvia's State Border Guard says it has opened 179 criminal proceedings against 121 people this year for moving people illegally across the border or enabling illegal stay. In one case on 10 November in Ludza region, border guards stopped a car driven by a Belarusian citizen with seven people inside who had crossed from Belarus. New penalties of up to 12 years in prison for organising illegal migration took effect in early November.
corroboration: Reported by LSM from the border guard; the car case was published on 11 November and is not counted as new today.
analysis: The figure is higher than the 138 smuggling cases in our earlier editions because it also covers enabling illegal stay. It shows that much of the pressure on Latvia continues past the border as organised onward transport.

title: 2027 solidarity pool still undecided; Latvia reportedly seeks a revised assessment
summary: The Council has not yet set the 2027 solidarity pool. Several outlets report that Latvia's interior minister has asked the Commission to revise its 2027 migration assessment, arguing that prevented crossing attempts were not counted. We could not open these reports, so the date and details are unverified.
corroboration: Seen only in headlines from several outlets; no official text checked.
analysis: If confirmed, Latvia is seeking recognition of greater pressure, which would mean more support and fewer obligations, not more migrants. Nothing in the process obliges a Baltic state to accept relocated people.

title: Human rights court: returns to Belarus not unlawful in themselves, but violations in all three cases
summary: On 24 November the European Court of Human Rights' Grand Chamber ruled on pushbacks at the Belarus border in 2021–2022. It found that Belarus's instrumentalisation of migration was a deliberate threat to the states, and that returning people to the instrumentalising state is not in itself a breach of Article 3, but that authorities must identify children and others with evident vulnerabilities or a real risk of ill-treatment. Poland breached Article 3 by removing one man despite an interim measure, and blocked lawyers' access (€20,000 and €5,000 awarded). Latvia breached Article 3 for children and their families, over border-zone conditions, and unlawfully detained the children. In Lithuania's case the court found no Article 3 breach, by 11 votes to 6, but unanimously found the four applicants' six-month detention unlawful and awarded €15,000 each.
corroboration: Holdings from the court's own press release; reported by Euronews, dpa, LRT/BNS and Notes from Poland. Coverage differs on emphasis, not on facts.
analysis: The ruling gives governments legal room to deal with instrumentalised crossings while keeping a duty to screen individuals. It does not approve automatic pushbacks of everyone, nor does it ban returns to Belarus.

title: Governments welcome the ruling; rights groups condemn it
summary: Poland's deputy interior minister called the judgments very important and favourable for Poland, saying the court in effect endorsed its approach to instrumentalisation. Amnesty International, which intervened in the Latvian and Lithuanian cases, called the rulings a devastating blow to legal certainty and the ban on torture, while stressing they are not a green light to bypass people's rights at borders. No reaction from the Latvian or Lithuanian governments was found.
corroboration: Polish reaction reported by Notes from Poland; Amnesty's statement on its own website.
analysis: Each side quotes the part it likes. The court's actual test, screening for vulnerability and real risk, sits between the two readings.

title: Latvia asks the Commission to treat it as under considerable pressure
summary: LSM, citing the interior ministry, reports that Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava wrote to the Commission asking it to reassess Latvia for 2027 as a state under considerable migratory pressure, to take account of instrumentalisation and prevented crossing attempts, and to consider the cost of receiving Ukrainian refugees. The ministry also opposes Latvia's share of the solidarity pool and seeks an exemption. The Commission has promised to count prevented attempts from the 2028 cycle, after a joint letter in September from the interior ministers of Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, Poland and Finland.
corroboration: LSM report of 23 November based on the ministry's press information; confirms what earlier editions saw only in headlines.
analysis: Latvia is seeking more support and fewer obligations, not more migrants. The Council decides the pool by qualified majority.

title: Lithuania: about 26,500 people turned back since 2021
summary: LRT/BNS reports that Lithuania has turned back about 26,500 people at the Belarus border in total, nearly 2,000 in 2026, over 1,600 in 2025 and 1,002 in 2024. A Belarusian exile outlet reported earlier that Lithuania recorded no attempts on 15–17 November while Latvia recorded 76.
corroboration: Figures from the State Border Guard Service as reported by BNS and Reform.news.
analysis: Lithuania's 2026 total is above last year's but far below Latvia's, which confirms that pressure has shifted north. These are attempts, not individual people.

title: Estonia's Russia border closure: 'indefinite in substance'
summary: Prime Minister Kristen Michal told ERR the road-crossing closure from 1 December is officially temporary but in substance indefinite, and closing the Narva rail crossing could follow. Estonia's interior ministry has earlier described a possible Russian push of migrants toward the closed border as a contingency.
corroboration: ERR interview; no unusual movement on the Russian side reported.
analysis: The closure is a security response to sabotage, not a migration measure. A migrant push from Russia remains a scenario, not an observed trend.
